extracted.intended_audience: inventors and patent applicants preparing a Malaysian patent specification (MyIPO guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for drafting a complete patent specification (Description, Claims, Abstract, Drawings, Sequence Listing) suitable for filing with MyIPO, including formality requirements, claim drafting rules, and filing preparations. Geared toward inventors/new applicants preparing their own specification (not a substitute for a patent agent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification components
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete specification is made up of Description, Claims, Abstract and Drawings (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parts form the document on which a patent, if granted, is based. Each part must start on a new page. Ensure all components are present and consistent with one another before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must enable at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must explain your invention fully at the time of filing because information cannot be added later. A patent will not be granted if your description does not contain sufficient information to enable others to construct or perform your invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the description with enough technical detail and examples so a person skilled in the art can carry out the invention. Do not rely on later amendments to add essential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must indicate clearly and concisely the subject matter of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, direct titles (e.g., 'A TOOTHBRUSH'). Ensure consistency between the title and the independent claim preamble (function/purpose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Field
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the art or technology to which the invention relates and be consistent with the preamble of the independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested phrasings: 'The present invention relates generally to ...' or 'The present invention relates generally to ..., particularly ...'. Do not include statements about advantages or the inventive concept here; save those for the Detailed Description of the Preferred Embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any prior art useful for understanding the invention by discussing disadvantages or problems with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly describe relevant prior devices/systems and their drawbacks. Avoid discussing the advantages of your invention here; that belongs in the Detailed Description or Summary of the Invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the solution provided by the invention and the advantageous effects compared to the stated prior art; usually a repetition of the broadest claim and dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is advisable to draft claims first and then prepare the summary. Use comprehensive sentences starting with 'According to the present invention, ...' for independent-claim-equivalent text and 'In an embodiment ...' for dependent-claim-equivalent text. Insert all claims as sentences that describe the invention concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Description of the Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: List the relevant figures with a brief one-sentence explanation for each, starting with an overall view then more detailed figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include suggested views such as perspective, plan/top, front, side, exploded, rear and cross-sectional. Arrange figures so Figure 1 shows the overall embodiment, Figure 2 shows operation, then detailed parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed Description of the Preferred Embodiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the embodiment(s) in great detail, including technical features, interconnections, how it is operated, and advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the listed drawings (e.g., 'Referring to Figure 1 ...'). Describe each technical feature with its reference number, connections and operation. Explain alternative embodiments and emphasize advantages at the end. Close with a statement that changes and modifications may be made within the invention's broadest aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference numbering practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each technical feature in the description must be followed by a reference number accordingly; adopt consistent numbering conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good practice: start with two-digit (20,22,24) or three-digit (110,112,114) numbers and choose only even or only odd numbering (e.g., 21,23,25) so new numbers can be inserted between related numbers. Use the same reference numbers in description, claims, abstract and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Embodiments are different variations of the same inventive concept, used to maximize the scope of protection claimed in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe multiple embodiments to cover variations. Use dependent claims to capture particular embodiments and examples to illustrate scope and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims determine scope and must meet core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims determine the scope of the monopoly. Claims must define the subject matter to be protected, be clear and concise, and be fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each claim's technical features have been described earlier. Avoid ambiguity: the meaning should be clear to a person skilled in the art from the wording of the claim alone. Consistency between description and claims is vital to avoid unclarity or lack of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims drafted in technical terms (no commercial matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be drafted in terms of the technical features of the invention; claims should not contain statements relating to commercial advantages or other non-technical matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of purpose are allowed if they assist in defining the invention. Always prefer technical feature wording and ensure support in the description for each claimed feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent claim represents the broadest claim, stands alone (does not refer to any preceding claim) and must include all essential technical features of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all elements indispensable for providing the effect and solving the technical problem. Draft so the claim recites enough features that the invention can work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim depends on another claim, must reference the depended claim at the beginning, contains all features of the independent claim plus further features, and may only narrow the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft dependent claims to describe particular embodiments and further limitations. They must not broaden the scope of the claim they depend upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of claims and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional fees will be imposed for the number of claims exceeding 10 (fees escalate with claim count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of per-claim fee schedule (e.g., specific RM amounts for claim ranges). For utility innovation applications only one claim is allowed. Plan claim drafting with fee implications in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a one-paragraph summary (recommended up to 150 words) indicating the technical field, the technical problem, the solution and the principal use of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract is often based on the independent claim but not always helpful as a verbatim claim. Include the most relevant figure and use the same reference numbers for technical features as elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a figure showing the overall preferred embodiment, then figures showing operation and detailed parts; label technical features in drawings with the same reference numbers used in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label the technical feature defined in the technical field with an arrow while other features without arrow. Arrange figures in a logical order (overall view first, operation second, details following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings execution standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be executed in durable, black, sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined lines and strokes without colouring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coloured drawings are not allowed. Ensure clarity and durability of lines; use clear reference numerals on drawings matching the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing and biological sequence disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For sequences, the application must indicate industrial applicability; a mere nucleic acid sequence without indication of a function is not patentable. If the sequence is used to produce a protein, specify which protein/part and its function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the nucleotide sequence is not used to produce a protein, indicate another function (e.g., promoter activity). Ensure sequence listings follow prescribed format and include required functional data to demonstrate industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality requirements: sheet, drawing, and sequence numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets excluding drawings and sequence listings shall be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals [1,2,3...]; drawings and sequence listings shall be numbered as separate series ([1/n, 2/n,...] and [SQL n,...] respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place numbering at the top and in the middle of each sheet. Maintain separate numbering series for description/claims, drawings, and sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality requirements: line numbering, margins, spacing and text
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fifth line of each sheet of the description and claims shall be numbered [5,10,15...]. Minimum margins of sheets shall be 2 cm (left, right, top and bottom). Text must be typed/printed in dark indelible colour with at least 1½ line spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conform strictly to these formatting rules to avoid formality objections. Ensure line numbering is legible and consistent across sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality requirement: part separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part of the specification (Description, Claims, Abstract, Drawings) shall start on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear page breaks and headings for each part so examiners and filing systems can process the application correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing preparation and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing prepare forms (Form 1 or Form 14, Form 17 if any, Form 22 if any) and the specification; for online filing prepare all documents in separate files and upload individual parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted attachment formats: DOC, PDF or TIF. Ensure each part of the specification is a separate file for upload. Include any agent appointment or right-to-patent statements as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical drafting sequence advice
rubrics_metrics.description: It is advisable to start with drafting the claims first then followed by other subcomponents of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims define the invention's scope; writing claims first helps ensure consistency across the Summary, Detailed Description, Abstract and Drawings and avoids unsupported claim features.
